I am writing to urge the City Council to vote against lifting the SLCPD hiring freeze. You cite the increase in crime as motivation for turning back on the promises to our community to decrease reliance on police in our community, however 2020 was the 3rd lowest in crime rate out of the last 7 years in SLC. Furthermore, every article explaining 2020's increase in crime since the previous year attributes it to the pandemic, a problem that will not be solved by the police. Police spokesperson Keith Horrocks himself said it takes about 18 months to train new officers and get them prepared to work a shift on their own. Lifting the hiring freeze will not fix this issue quickly, or at all. Chief Mike Brown has stated the police are the most expensive and probably the least effective at addressing our community's struggle with mental health, substance use, or homelessness. So why do we keep putting them up to the job with no power to fix these issues only to put our community in danger of continued police violence? There is no quick fix to this. Let's stop throwing our money at the police and instead invest in long-term solutions to community safety - increasing access to basic needs including housing, healthcare, mental health and substance use services. Vote to maintain the hiring freeze and continue to shift resources and responsibility from the police towards meaningful, long-term community support.

But I am concerned that the hiring freeze is an inadequate way to get there. I do think there needs to be done more for crime prevention and I would love to see the city move towards a prevention model such as the Cure Violence methodology being used in cities across the country. Can the city look at alternative hiring and training practices that can be working toward racial equity? I think we are having issues getting the current victims cases resolved and I'm not sure how a hiring freeze will help that. I would prefer the police work towards increasing community policing, partnering with social workers and community advocates to address complex issues like mental health,and solving cases more quickly thru established relationships with community members, but I don't think extending the hiring freeze is good policy. Thanks for your work to represent us. Hope you're well and safe. Stephanie Burdick

The city should support these, of course, but the #1 responsibility of the city government is the protection of the citizens. This is the biggest issue my neighbors and I face in Marmalade. We deal with crime almost on a daily basis. Our property is stolen or vandalized frequently. We also see open air drug dealing constantly. We have learned that when we call the police on anything that is not life/death, we will not have a police response. Simply unacceptable. One of my best friends just moved out of Marmalade for Davis County because his home was broken into while he was in it and the police did not show up for an hour. You have a lot of voices to listen to, and I understand there is a real need to have a more diverse and reformed police department, but crime has taken over our city and you did the right thing by moving to hire more officers. Thank you for your courage in doing this. Please continue to prioritize public safety Kevin Fawkes Marmalade resident

I've also heard that the west, North Temple area is as bad or worse. Crime is the number 1 issue for the people living in these neighborhoods. What matters more when a person hears gunshots next door and has drug dealers across the street? I applaud your decision to lift the hiring freeze for the Police Department. The police officers are our true heroes. They put their lives on the line for us, as citizens, every day. Defunding the police was an experiment that has not worked. Our city is not safer because of it. Last summer, there was talk about increasing training for the police. That would be good, but it takes money. And if the police are understaffed, there is no time for training. I encourage you to increase funding for the police, even beyond their budget from before they were defunded. Each of us deserves a peaceful neighborhood in which to live. And that requires a sufficient number of well trained police officers. Thank you for your service. Rob Udarbe
